subject: Evidence handoff & validation: EU operational roles / keystore operator scope
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@orbitalhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@orbitalhealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 15:22:00 +01:00
Subject: CAIQ/SIG slice + operator roster for EU edge nodes

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement at Orbital needs a compact CAIQ/SIG slice focused on residency + ops controls for the EU footprint, plus an operator roster that maps which roles can perform privatelink/peering and keystore operations for EU edge zones. Specifically we need:

- A CAIQ/SIG excerpt that highlights data residency, VPC isolation, peering/privatelink controls, and keystore management (we're fine with redacted artifact links).
- A CSV or similar that lists operator roles, role descriptions, and whether they require MFA/HSM access to perform keystore operations (we'll mask names if necessary).
- Any runbook or playbook describing how keystore operator handoffs/rotations are performed for EU nodes (HSM partitioning, escrow processes).

Target: we'd like these by EOD Wednesday (European business hours) to feed into our SOC procurement review. If you need a narrower scope or an alternative delivery mechanism (dataroom vs Drive link), let me know — procurement prefers minimal, digestible artifacts rather than the full SOC pack.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang
Security & Compliance, Orbital Health
claire.huang@orbitalhealth.com

Subject: Re: CAIQ/SIG slice + operator roster for EU edge nodes

Marissa — thanks, this looks good from a scope perspective. A couple quick clarifications before we mark the packet as complete for procurement:

1) On the "mfa_required" column: can you confirm whether there are any service accounts that bypass MFA for keystore ops (we need explicit confirmation that no unattended accounts have keystore privileges without HSM gating).
2) HSM partitioning: the manifest mentions partitions per edge cluster — can you confirm whether the partitioning is implemented with physical separation (different HSM instances) or logical partitions on shared HSMs? If logical, please include the mitigation / compensating controls note.

If you can append a one-paragraph statement addressing those two bullets to the Drive folder, procurement will accept the packet and close the security review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Claire

On Wed, Mar 7, 2028 at 09:35 AM -07:00 jonas.weber@redwood.com wrote:
> Claire — quick note:
> 
> 1) No service accounts have unfettered keystore privileges. All keystore management operations require an operator identity bound to an MFA session and a keyed HSM operator certificate. We will add an explicit sentence to the manifest and CSV noting zero privileged unattended accounts for keystore ops.
> 2) HSM partitioning for EU edge: implemented via logical partitions on clustered HSMs with strict tenant mapping + hardware-backed wrapping keys per partition. Compensating controls include per-partition audit streams, scheduled key material rotation, and mandatory escrow to an EU-only escrow HSM. We'll add the mitigation paragraph to the runbook appendix.
> 
> I'll update the Drive folder now and paste the updated link once uploaded.
> 
> Jonas
